DNOW is the most energy-specific small/mid-cap candidate found in this pass, with supply-chain services, digital procurement, PVF/pumps/equipment distribution, gas utility, downstream, energy evolution, and industrial exposure.

For this node, the chokepoint is likely less about owning scarce physical equipment and more about qualification, availability, procurement workflow, inventory visibility, supplier networks, and project-critical distribution reliability.

node: Energy supplier-risk intelligence, procurement analytics, inspection, certification, and supply-chain assurance
summary: Layer 1B expands a non-obvious energy supply-chain assurance node. The strongest public-market mappings are not pure supplier-risk-intelligence software names, because several obvious platforms are private or have been taken private. The investable lane therefore shifts toward testing/certification gates, electrical and utility distribution, energy-specific supply-chain services, and MRO/procurement platforms that help utilities, EPCs, developers, and energy operators secure constrained or qualified equipment. The candidate set deliberately includes one reference distributor and three more node-relevant underfollowed names.
